body.estimand_functional: The established observational result is the all-regime bracket \(c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\le\rho_n^*\le C n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) when \(d\le4t\), and \(c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\le\rho_n^*\le C n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) when \(d>4t\), where \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\). In particular, if \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\) and \(d\le4\gamma\), then \(\rho_n^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\). The complete critical-radius map remains the target of \(\texttt{oeq:complete-frontier}\); no common rate is defined from the invalid frozen testing and mixture handles.

sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed observed margins of a law in \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A\) has unknown propensity \(e\) under the observational experiment; the comparison experiment supplies the exact function \(e_P\) to the test.
sampling_model.outcome: Observed and potential outcomes are binary. The pointwise restrictions \(m_0,m_1\in[1/4,3/4]\) apply to the canonical continuous representatives of the two conditional-mean equivalence classes.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator and no nuisance convergence rate is part of the class; all tuning is a deterministic function of \(n,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives the pointwise CATE-estimation minimax rate with a nuisance-smoothness elbow, and Theorem 2 gives attainability under additional design-density conditions.
Theorems 4 and 6 give fixed-alternative consistency and a local weak limit for quantitative homogeneity tests over structured rule classes under the paper's nuisance conditions.

Theorems 1--2 establish asymptotic normality for propensity-reweighted pairwise and multisample adjusted \(U\)-statistics under consistent propensity estimation, independent stratum samples, stable positive sample fractions, and pointwise overlap.

Section 3 derives joint asymptotic normality and Gaussian-simulation calibration for multisample \(U\)-statistics testing equality of additive treatment effects across a fixed collection of mutually independent prespecified strata.

Theorem 6 gives asymptotic level, fixed-alternative consistency, and nontrivial \(n^{-1/2}\)-local power for a multiplier-bootstrap test of homogeneous restricted CATE with possibly right-censored duration outcomes.

Section 4 gives a conservative finite-sample-valid Fisher randomization test for the sharp null of one unknown constant individual treatment effect by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over a confidence set for that nuisance effect.

The main martingale-transformation results give asymptotic level for a permutation test of a constant marginal-distribution shift with an estimated nuisance shift, retaining exact level only for the more restrictive sharp null.
Theorems 3 and 7 give asymptotic chi-square tests of equality of finitely many score-defined group average treatment effects under complete randomization, with sample splitting or cross-fitting.
Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 give matching nonasymptotic binned conditional-independence critical radii for fixed discrete responses and a continuous conditioning variable under total-variation smoothness.
Theorems 6 and 7 give null validity and spline minimax power for projected conditional covariance under common smoothness and nondegeneracy restrictions.
Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 characterize bias, variance, and optimal separate wavelet resolutions for estimating a signed expected conditional covariance functional.
The main minimax theorems derive sharp heteroskedasticity-detection rates using a squared first-difference proxy under a rough unknown mean.
Theorem 1 gives asymptotic normality and type-I error control for an intra-fold split CATE-variance statistic under explicit nuisance learner-rate conditions.
The paper proves that the propensity score is ancillary for semiparametrically efficient estimation of the regular average treatment effect under ignorability.
Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 give asymptotic null validity and consistency against smooth local sieve alternatives for the null that the conditional average treatment effect is constant.

The paper develops \(L_1\)-type tests based on uniformly consistent nonparametric kernel estimators for conditional treatment-effect restrictions and proves asymptotically correct size, fixed-alternative consistency, and power against some local alternatives.
Section 1 records the classical nonadaptive Hölder goodness-of-fit boundary, and the paper establishes the iterated-logarithmic price of adaptation in wavelet testing.

body.tldr: The known-propensity experiment has the standard nonadaptive radius \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\). For the observational experiment, an explicit profiled fourth-order statistic gives a uniform finite-sample all-regime upper bound and matches the known-propensity rate when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\) and \(d\le4\gamma\). The originally frozen multiresolution testing and null-mixture envelopes are regression-test failures, not candidate sharp rates: the former mishandles the signal-dependent first Hoeffding projection, and the latter omits an unavoidable degree-two likelihood term involving the CATE amplitude. The exact repaired local likelihood expansion is now available and rules out the spurious lower obstruction at \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,9/10)\), but the sharp two-scale prior and matching sparse-regime corrected-energy test remain unproved. Accordingly the paper currently delivers a rigorous bracket and a matched no-penalty region; it does not yet name \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\), claim the complete frontier, claim smoothness adaptation, certify a fitted forest, or interpret non-rejection as homogeneity.

project_justification.gap: Published CATE-homogeneity procedures establish asymptotic validity or power under structured directions and nuisance learner conditions; published minimax results instead treat pointwise CATE estimation, conditional independence under different geometry, signed expected covariance, or heteroskedasticity. None gives the fixed-sample critical radius over the identical binary causal class with three separate Hölder indices and an unknown constant null.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the rough-confounding testing modulus itself, including sparse occupancy, asymmetric propensity and baseline smoothness, boundary logarithms, and the statistical value of revealing the true propensity.
project_justification.fill: The proved analysis uses an exact binned covariance identity and a profiled fourth-order statistic to obtain a uniformly calibrated observational upper bound, together with the known-propensity minimax converse to form an honest all-regime bracket. The lower-handle audit now starts from complete binary cell probabilities and an exact prior-predictive product: it proves that every positive induced CATE amplitude creates an unavoidable degree-two discrepancy, so no tenth-power remainder can hide a CATE-only path. Completing the paper requires a new two-scale same-class null-supported prior and a matching multiresolution covariance-correction test; the invalid frozen optimizations are not used to define the answer.

exactness is retained only for the sharper known-shift null.\\ Imai--Li (2025) & Iid units with complete randomization and an external or split-sample score & A fixed number of score-defined group average effects are equal & Finite-dimensional GATE contrasts & Theorems 3 and 7 give asymptotic chi-square calibration, not an omnibus continuous-CATE guarantee.\\ Dukes et al. (2026) & Observational causal model with a structured rule class and estimated nuisances & Quantitative CATE homogeneity over that rule class & Structured policy-direction contrasts & Theorems 2, 4, and 6 give asymptotic size, fixed power, and local weak limits.\\ Yu (2026) & Observational causal model with learner-rate and nondegeneracy conditions & \(\operatorname{Var}\{\tau(X)\}=0\) & Fixed positive CATE variance & Theorem 1 is asymptotic and assumes nuisance rates.\\ Chang et al. (2015) & Unconfounded treatment with kernel conditional-mean estimators & Zero, nonpositive, or distributional conditional-effect restrictions & \(L_1\)-type fixed and local alternatives & Asymptotically correct size and consistency only.\\ NBW (2021) & Discrete responses and a continuous conditioner with conditional-law smoothness & Conditional independence & Total-variation distance to the null class & Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 give nonasymptotic minimax bounds in a different model.\\ PCM (2024) & Conditional-mean model with spline regressions and common smoothness & Conditional mean independence & Squared projected conditional mean & Theorems 6--7 give uniform asymptotic, not finite-sample, guarantees. \end{tabular}\end{center} SantAnna2021, Section 4.2 and Theorem 6, is the closest continuous-covariate extension of the Crump constant-CATE null, but its censored-duration integrated moments and root-\(n\) directional alternatives do not define a three-index Hölder minimax radius. DaiStern2022, Section 3, and DaiShenStern2023, Theorems 1--2, compare average effects across a fixed finite stratum geometry; neither tests arbitrary variation over the full-support cube nor provides uniform finite-sample calibration. DingFellerMiratrix2016 supplies exact-design validity for a sharper unit-level constant-effect null, ChungOlivares2021 supplies asymptotic distribution-shift permutation validity, and ImaiLi2025 tests equality of finitely many score-defined GATEs; these nulls can respectively be stronger than, different from, or coarser than continuous CATE constancy. CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008 remains the closest uncensored unknown-constant-CATE predecessor, but its series asymptotics do not furnish the present fixed-sample radius. ChangLeeWhang2015 and DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026 establish asymptotic conditional-effect tests under kernel or structured-rule formulations. Yu2026VarianceHTE studies the same variance-zero characterization under supplied learner rates. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 concerns pointwise CATE estimation; its loss and support-modified lower construction do not solve global homogeneity testing. NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 and LundborgKimShahSamworth2024 supply testing machinery under different null manifolds and metrics. McGrathMukherjee2026 informs separate nuisance resolutions for a signed covariance functional, and KotekalKundu2025 informs rough-regression proxy design under a Gaussian likelihood. Spokoiny1996 supplies only the known-propensity goodness-of-fit benchmark, and Hahn1998 supplies only the regular ATE ancillarity comparator.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For a bounded local pair \((U,V)\), exact one-observation matching can induce an alternative CATE perturbation \(4\delta B^2\), where \(\delta=\mathbb E_0(UV)-\mathbb E_1(UV)\). However, the \(B(x_i)B(x_j)\) coefficient of the two-observation prior predictive law is \(r_{s_i}^{\top}(\Sigma_0-\Sigma_1)r_{s_j}\). The binary-row score vectors span \(\mathbb R^2\), so cancelling all such coefficients forces \(\Sigma_0=\Sigma_1\) and hence \(\delta=0\). A valid lower envelope must therefore charge \((n)_2M^{-d}\delta^2\). At \((1,1,1/10,9/10)\), balancing this term with the legal one-scale amplitude gives \(n^{-2/3}\), below the established oracle obstruction \(n^{-2/5}\), so the frozen \(n^{-5/14}\) artifact disappears. At the early-kill point \((1,1,1/10,1/10)\), one scale cannot simultaneously use the nuisance-product amplitude and preserve a Lipschitz CATE; the unresolved lower construction must separate micro nuisance cells from a smooth macro effect. The matching upper construction must estimate and remove within-signal-cell nuisance covariance while deriving every sparse-occupancy Hoeffding projection.
body.honest_scope: The causal class, binary outcomes, exact uniform design, overlap, three separate fixed H"older indices, and unknown constant null are unchanged. Established results are the known-propensity radius, the total single-scale profiled test, the observational all-regime bracket, and equality with the known-propensity order when \(\alpha+\beta\ge\gamma\) and \(d\le4\gamma\), including \(n^{-1/4}\) without a logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\). The complete rough-nuisance radius, its transition logarithms, and the necessary-and-sufficient propensity-equality region remain open. The symbols and formulas of the frozen failed testing and mixture handles do not define the critical radius, and \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) remains undefined. Smoothness adaptation, unknown covariate density, outcomes outside \(\{0,1\}\), local overlap, and validation of any existing forest remain outside scope.
